mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: The Moon cannot totally eclipse the Sun because it is physically smaller than the Sun.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: A solar eclipse occurs whenever the Moon is on the Sun-facing side of Earth, even if its shadow misses Earth.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: A total solar eclipse is visible everywhere on Earth's sunlit half at once.

mx.name: mechanism_conflation
mx.teacher_note: A solar eclipse occurs when Earth comes between the Sun and Moon and Earth's shadow falls on the Moon.

intelligence.enrichment: During a solar eclipse, the Moon can block the Sun because the Moon and Sun have similar apparent sizes when viewed from Earth, even though the Moon is physically much smaller and much closer. Moon between Sun and Earth plus similar apparent size makes the Moon's shadow fall on Earth, producing total eclipse where sunlight is fully blocked and partial eclipse where only part of the Sun is blocked. The learner correctly applies this rule: During a solar eclipse, the Moon can block the Sun because the Moon and Sun have similar apparent sizes when viewed from Earth, even though the Moon is physically much smaller and much closer. A solar eclipse is any case where something passes near the Sun in the sky.
